items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: And so he came in and he knew me from when I was a trumpet player. And he said to me... His name is Michael Gribrock. And he’s still a really good friend of mine.

ctx.x: Playing guitar. And so I was starting to make a meager existence playing music. But the one thing that I realized was that — I kept on thinking well if I get the chops together I’ll start enjoying it as much as trumpet. Well I started developing technique and I got so that I could play it okay. But I never liked it as much. And it was only at the time when I started to get kind of a little bit proficient that I realized that there are some things that always bothered me about the guitar after playing the trumpet,…
That first time after, picking up the trumpet after ten years, did your chops remember what it felt like? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
